declared.title: High income improves evaluation of life but not emotional well-being
declared.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « high income improves evaluation of life but not emotional well-being » (2026-11-22)

population: US residents, more than 450,000 responses to the Gallup-Healthways daily poll (1,000 people a day)

findings.text: Judgement of one's life keeps rising with income, by the same step for each doubling, with no plateau in sight

support.sentence: When plotted against log income, life evaluation rises steadily.

findings.text: Life evaluation shows no satiation with income, at least up to well over $120,000 a year

support.sentence: In contrast, the figure shows a fairly steady rise in life evaluation with log income over the entire range; the effects of income on individuals’ life evaluations show no satiation, at least to an amount well over $120,000.
support.readBy: dossier agent (money-happiness), PNAS full text (reviewer's PMC copy), Results

findings.text: Day-to-day emotional well-being rises with income too, but stops improving above about $75,000 a year

support.sentence: Emotional well-being also rises with log income, but there is no further progress beyond an annual income of ~$75,000.

findings.text: The authors conclude that high income buys life satisfaction but not day-to-day happiness, and that low income goes with both being low

support.sentence: We conclude that high income buys life satisfaction but not happiness, and that low income is associated both with low life evaluation and low emotional well-being.

limits: cross-sectional: an association between income and well-being, not an effect of money
emotions measured by yes/no questions about yesterday: a ceiling effect, admitted by Kahneman himself in Killingsworth 2023
US only (2008-2009); household income in bands, not adjusted for local cost of living
its $75,000 is about emotions; its authors later place that threshold at $100,000 and only for the least happy (Killingsworth 2023, 2024)
